outlook.body:
- Deepen participation in India's circular economy by closing the loop across collection, recycling and production, reducing dependence on imported critical metals and strengthening domestic resource security
- Complete the London Metal Exchange listing under 'Ardee Lead 9997' to establish international credibility and global price benchmarking, complementing the existing MCX listing
- Grow the export franchise from the Tirupati facility's port proximity, building on presence in seven countries as of March 31, 2025
- Shift mix further towards higher-value customisable lead alloys tailored to customer-specific purity and composition requirements
- Continue sustainability-led cost and efficiency initiatives - oxygen enrichment during manufacturing to cut furnace oil dependence and green fuel derived from end-of-life tyres in place of coal and oil

outlook.body: Since the present Promoters acquired the Company in 2021, Ardee has invested continuously in its single owned Manufacturing Facility on approximately 7.61 acres at Naidupet, District Tirupati, Andhra Pradesh, raising installed recycling capacity from 54,750 MTPA in Fiscal 2023 (unchanged in Fiscal 2024) to 104,025 MTPA in Fiscal 2025. Manufacturing capital expenditure was INR 252.98 million in Fiscal 2025, INR 205.36 million in Fiscal 2024 and INR 220.29 million in Fiscal 2023, funding rotary furnaces, refining kettles, casting machines, pollution control systems and an in-house testing laboratory. The site was chosen for proximity to large lead-acid battery manufacturers such as Amara Raja Energy & Mobility (short turnaround, lower logistics cost) and to Chennai, Kattupalli and Ennore ports for import of scrap and export of finished lead, with National Highway 16 / Golden Quadrilateral connectivity. Market expansion has run alongside capacity: exports reached seven countries and domestic sales ten states as of March 31, 2025. Notably, the Fresh Issue proceeds are earmarked for working capital and debt repayment rather than a new plant - no further capacity addition project is quantified in this Draft Red Herring Prospectus.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Mix shift from pure lead to higher-value lead alloys - lead alloys rose from 17.18% of revenue from operations in Fiscal 2023 to 34.15% in Fiscal 2024 and 43.02% in Fiscal 2025, while pure lead fell from 70.51% to 42.34%
- Gross margin per ton expanded from INR 19,511.95 in Fiscal 2023 to INR 29,466.73 in Fiscal 2024 and INR 33,642.16 in Fiscal 2025, lifting EBITDA margin from 5.53% to 6.06% to 8.88%
- Export-led growth - export revenue CAGR of 521.22% from Fiscal 2023 to Fiscal 2025, with export share of revenue from operations rising from 1.73% to 17.63% to 37.03%
- Raw material sourcing shift towards imported scrap - import operations rose from 23.05% in Fiscal 2023 to 64.73% in Fiscal 2025, contingent on timely MoEFCC licences and approvals
- Working capital intensity is the dominant funding need - INR 2,200.00 million of the INR 3,200.00 million Fresh Issue is for incremental working capital
- Rising leverage - total borrowings grew from INR 809.08 million in Fiscal 2023 to INR 1,423.60 million in Fiscal 2024 and INR 1,657.66 million in Fiscal 2025 against net worth of INR 626.01 million in Fiscal 2025; INR 220.00 million of Net Proceeds is for repayment/pre-payment
- Cost levers from sustainability practices - oxygen incorporation during manufacturing reduces furnace oil dependence and green fuel from end-of-life tyres replaces coal and oil, enhancing productivity and optimising costs
- Capital efficiency improved - ROCE moved 19.77% (FY23) to 12.83% (FY24) to 25.17% (FY25) and RONW 42.38% to 30.61% to 53.15%, on a broadly steady fixed asset turnover of 10.44x, 10.22x and 11.15x
- Declining but still extreme customer concentration - top customer share fell from 85.73% (FY23) to 72.42% (FY24) to 51.22% (FY25); top 5 from 94.49% to 90.54% to 82.46%
- Lead price exposure managed through a hedging mechanism for commodity price risk and MCX benchmark pricing

other_material_facts.label: working_capital

(iv) Maximum utilization of installed capacity: We plan to maximise the utilisation of its installed capacity to meet growing demand.

concerns_observed: EVERY figure in this analysis is drawn from a draft dated September 28, 2025 whose newest fiscal year is FY25 (year ended March 31, 2025). The issue opened August 5, 2026 and closes August 7, 2026; an RHP dated July 27, 2026 exists and we do not hold it. A full financial year (FY26) has closed since these numbers were struck, and the DRHP itself carries no stub or interim period at all. Nothing here should be read as the company's current state.

Extreme customer concentration with no contractual protection: the top customer alone was 51.22% of FY25 revenue (Rs 3,804.08 million), 72.42% in FY24 and 85.73% in FY23; top 5 were 82.46% / 90.54% / 94.49%. The DRHP states there are no long-term customer agreements - orders arrive by e-mail against internal work orders. Battery and metal end-uses together were 87.23% of FY25 revenue.

Profit is not converting to cash. FY25 CFO was Rs 78.40 million against PAT of Rs 332.71 million; CFO was negative in both prior years (Rs -252.62 million FY24, Rs -137.66 million FY23) and investing cash flow was negative in all three (Rs -228.66 / -272.02 / -248.13 million). Operations and capex were funded by financing inflows of Rs 133.43 / 543.52 / 378.05 million. The DRHP flags this itself as Risk Factor 17.

The working-capital object rests on a projection that nearly triples the base: net working capital requirement goes from Rs 1,481.76 million actual (FY25) to Rs 1,872.80 million (FY26 projected) to Rs 4,182.47 million (FY27 projected), of which Rs 2,200.00 million comes from Net Proceeds. The FY27 leap is driven by advance-to-supplier days rising from 26 (FY25 actual) to 53, on a planned shift of import payment terms from Cash Against Documents to Free on Board, and trade payable days falling from 15 (FY26E) to 4 (FY27E). The projection was certified by Mohan Gupta & Company (certificate dated September 26, 2025) - the firm that resigned as statutory auditor on March 24, 2025.

Group Company Pilot Industries Limited converges on the company from six directions at once: it is a named Group Company; it is in a similar business (conflict addressed only by a Non-Compete Agreement dated September 1, 2025 running three years); it is a raw-material supplier in which Chairman and Managing Director Sandeep Aggarwal is a shareholder and director; it is the largest related-party counterparty (FY25 loan received Rs 295.00 million and loan repaid Rs 295.00 million; purchase of goods Rs 93.21 / 141.64 / 82.26 million and sale of goods Rs 81.28 / 78.56 / 233.79 million across FY25 / FY24 / FY23); it is the former employer of VP-Operations Amitabh Agrawal; and it is a named accused in both criminal proceedings disclosed against the Promoters.

Capital was engineered immediately before the Offer. A 15:1 bonus on August 14, 2025 created 238,897,500 of the 254,824,000 pre-Offer shares, following a July 2025 sub-division of Rs 100 shares into Rs 2 shares. Weighted average cost of acquisition for all shareholders is Rs 0.00 over the last 3 years, 18 months and 1 year (range Rs 0.00-1.12); average cost of acquisition is Rs 0.20 per share for each of Sandeep Aggarwal and Nikunj Aggarwal. Both are also the Promoter Selling Shareholders in an Offer for Sale of up to 37,650,000 Equity Shares (18,825,000 each), the proceeds of which accrue entirely to them.

The DRHP's own Risk Factor 31 names a structural threat to both ends of the business at once: as the Indian battery market shifts to lithium-ion, the availability of used lead-acid batteries for recycling could decline over the medium to long term, and so could demand for pure lead and lead alloys. The DRHP characterises the raw-material supply-chain impact as a material risk.

Utilisation moved the wrong way as capacity doubled: total capacity utilisation fell from 59.48% (FY24) and 53.51% (FY23) to 45.16% (FY25); the pure-lead line alone fell from 43.51% (FY23) and 43.39% (FY24) to 30.07% (FY25). The governance layer is weeks old relative to the draft. The Promoters were identified as such by Board resolution dated July 18, 2025. The DRHP notes only one Director (Archana Jain) has prior listed-company board experience (Risk Factor 51).

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Mix shift from pure lead to higher-value lead alloys - lead alloys rose from 17.18% of revenue from operations in Fiscal 2023 to 34.15% in Fiscal 2024 and 43.02% in Fiscal 2025, while pure lead fell from 70.51% to 42.34%
- Gross margin per ton expanded from INR 19,511.95 in Fiscal 2023 to INR 29,466.73 in Fiscal 2024 and INR 33,642.16 in Fiscal 2025, lifting EBITDA margin from 5.53% to 6.06% to 8.88%
- Export-led growth - export revenue CAGR of 521.22% from Fiscal 2023 to Fiscal 2025, with export share of revenue from operations rising from 1.73% to 17.63% to 37.03%
- Raw material sourcing shift towards imported scrap - import operations rose from 23.05% in Fiscal 2023 to 64.73% in Fiscal 2025, contingent on timely MoEFCC licences and approvals
- Working capital intensity is the dominant funding need - INR 2,200.00 million of the INR 3,200.00 million Fresh Issue is for incremental working capital
- Rising leverage - total borrowings grew from INR 809.08 million in Fiscal 2023 to INR 1,423.60 million in Fiscal 2024 and INR 1,657.66 million in Fiscal 2025 against net worth of INR 626.01 million in Fiscal 2025; INR 220.00 million of Net Proceeds is for repayment/pre-payment
- Cost levers from sustainability practices - oxygen incorporation during manufacturing reduces furnace oil dependence and green fuel from end-of-life tyres replaces coal and oil, enhancing productivity and optimising costs
- Capital efficiency improved - ROCE moved 19.77% (FY23) to 12.83% (FY24) to 25.17% (FY25) and RONW 42.38% to 30.61% to 53.15%, on a broadly steady fixed asset turnover of 10.44x, 10.22x and 11.15x
- Declining but still extreme customer concentration - top customer share fell from 85.73% (FY23) to 72.42% (FY24) to 51.22% (FY25); top 5 from 94.49% to 90.54% to 82.46%
- Lead price exposure managed through a hedging mechanism for commodity price risk and MCX benchmark pricing

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: Since the present Promoters acquired the Company in 2021, Ardee has invested continuously in its single owned Manufacturing Facility on approximately 7.61 acres at Naidupet, District Tirupati, Andhra Pradesh, raising installed recycling capacity from 54,750 MTPA in Fiscal 2023 (unchanged in Fiscal 2024) to 104,025 MTPA in Fiscal 2025. Manufacturing capital expenditure was INR 252.98 million in Fiscal 2025, INR 205.36 million in Fiscal 2024 and INR 220.29 million in Fiscal 2023, funding rotary furnaces, refining kettles, casting machines, pollution control systems and an in-house testing laboratory. The site was chosen for proximity to large lead-acid battery manufacturers such as Amara Raja Energy & Mobility (short turnaround, lower logistics cost) and to Chennai, Kattupalli and Ennore ports for import of scrap and export of finished lead, with National Highway 16 / Golden Quadrilateral connectivity. Market expansion has run alongside capacity: exports reached seven countries and domestic sales ten states as of March 31, 2025. Notably, the Fresh Issue proceeds are earmarked for working capital and debt repayment rather than a new plant - no further capacity addition project is quantified in this Draft Red Herring Prospectus.

- Regulatory entry barrier advantage - lead scrap imports require MoEFCC licensing and stringent compliance; a proven compliance record has kept approvals timely, lifting import operations from 23.05% in Fiscal 2023 to 64.73% in Fiscal 2025
- Strategic plant location in Tirupati close to large lead-acid battery manufacturers such as Amara Raja Energy & Mobility, giving short turnaround times and lower logistics cost, and near Chennai (150 km), Kattupalli (130 km) and Ennore (130 km) ports for export/import
- Broad customisable product portfolio of pure lead plus five lead alloy families with purity from 99.97% to 99.985% conforming to international standards
- Brand 'Ardee' listed on MCX providing transparent benchmark pricing, hedging against price risk and market visibility; application filed for LME listing under 'Ardee Lead 9997'
- One of the fastest growing companies by revenue among its peers with a revenue CAGR of 33.15% over the last three Fiscals (Source: F&S Report)
- Strong customer base with robust raw material sourcing capability - 34, 29 and 14 repeat customers and 20, 25 and 28 new customers added in Fiscals 2025, 2024 and 2023
- Track record of profitability and consistent financial performance; experienced promoters and professional management team
- Application of a hedging mechanism for commodity price risk protection
